pull.title: feat(reasoning): effort floor 1024, adaptation warnings in log + dashboard, mandatory-model handling, dead-encoder removal
pull.body:
## What was broken

Four issues found by a research pass comparing this proxy's reasoning-effort handling against 20+ routers, gateways and native provider APIs (LiteLLM, OpenRouter, Helicone, Portkey, vLLM, OpenClaw, AI Proxy, llmgateway, Envoy, Vercel AI SDK, Pydantic AI, LangChain, Docker Agent + OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini/xAI/Bedrock natives). Full comparative write-up kept out of the repo (untracked scratch); the actionable gaps were:

- **R1 — effort floor invalid.** `_EFFORT_BUDGET_TOKENS` had MINIMAL/LOW at 512 tokens. Anthropic enforces `budget_tokens >= 1024` (hard 400 below that); every surveyed system floors at 1024. A 512-token thinking budget could only ever fail or be silently re-clamped downstream.
- **R2 — gating was silent.** `adapt_reasoning_policy` narrowed a requested policy against per-model capability (clamp, substitute, drop, suppress) but surfaced the reason only as a server log line. A client asking for "max" on a model topping out at "medium" could not learn why the request changed.
- **R3 — always-reasoning models were unhandled.** Models that cannot disable thinking (Claude Fable/Mythos-class, some Grok) would 400 on an explicit OFF, or silently get the provider's own floor with no signal.
- **R4 — dead encoder.** `GeminiReasoningEncoder` (providers/google_openai/reasoning.py) was defined and re-exported but never instantiated; the shipped Gemini path uses `NamedEffortReasoning` + `apply_gemini_request_quirks`. Dead code that looks like an unimplemented feature is a maintenance trap.

## The mechanism

- **R1:** MINIMAL/LOW 512 -> 1_024 in `core/reasoning.py`, with the regression baseline (`reasoning_request_baseline.json`) and the two stale NIM expectations updated to match. The client-visible budget ladder otherwise unchanged.
- **R2:** `adapt_reasoning_policy` returns `tuple[ReasoningPolicy, ReasoningAdaptation]`. New `ReasoningAdaptationKind` (UNCHANGED/SUBSTITUTED/CLAMPED/DROPPED/SUPPRESSED) + `ReasoningAdaptation(kind, message)` in `core/reasoning.py`. The adaptation threads routing (`RoutedMessagesRequest.reasoning_adaptation`) -> capture (`request_capture.py`) -> request log (schema column + guarded `ALTER TABLE` migration + INSERT + read) -> detail export (`export.py` field/order/label) -> dashboard (`admin.js` Thinking pane, `formatReasoningAdaptation`). NULL on ungated requests and pre-migration rows; "no warning" and "nobody recorded" are deliberately indistinguishable in storage, matching the `requested_reasoning` convention. A clamp+substitute chain merges into one descriptor at the worse of the two kinds.
- **R3:** `mandatory: bool | None = None` on `ModelReasoningCapability`, parsed from a conventional `reasoning_mandatory` models.dev key — **explicit True only**; absent stays None (unknown), so the "unknown changes nothing" invariant is preserved and a wrong True can never rewrite every OFF request. When mandatory is True and the client asks OFF, `_mandatory_off_rewrite` sends the lowest supported effort (or adaptive without a vocabulary) with a `REASONING OFF SUBSTITUTED` warning. **No models.dev entry publishes the key today, so this is ship-as-ready: zero behavior change until a source carries the flag.**
- **R4:** encoder + exclusive helper + re-export deleted; `test_adaptive_reasoning.py` gemini branch and the 35 `gemini|*` baseline keys removed. `VertexReasoningEncoder` (wired at `vertex/client.py:37`) untouched.

## What verification caught (and why the INSERT fix is in here)

The touched suites passed 345/345 **while the request-log INSERT carried 43 columns and 42 `?` placeholders** — every row write failed with `Request log write failed: 42 values for 43 columns`, cascading ~260 failures across `test_request_log*` and downstream, all hidden behind file-scoped green. The full-suite re-run and the repo-wide `ty check` (which also caught two fixtures missing the now-required `reasoning_adaptation` field) are what surfaced both. Fixed: the 43rd placeholder (script-asserted column-count == placeholder-count, not hand-typed) and the two fixtures. Lesson recorded in WORKING-NOTES §48.

## Verification (real output)

- Touched suites: `345 passed` (test_reasoning_gating.py, test_adaptive_reasoning.py, test_models_dev.py).
- Full suite: `18 failed, 5218 passed, 38 skipped in 830.98s`.
  - 16 of 18 are this environment's documented pre-existing set (PS1 installer x6, websearch registry/settings x8, CI-script suppression x2) — same failures on unmodified `main`.
  - The remaining 2 (`test_run_web_search_ddgs_failure_skips_second_ddgs_attempt`, `test_explicit_missing_credentials_surfaces_config_error`) are the §22 real-key class: they fail only because a real `EXA_API_KEY` sits in the shell env defeating `Settings()` isolation. Proven: with websearch keys stripped, `2 passed in 31.30s`.
- Full-repo `ty check`: `All checks passed!` (CI parity — file-scoped had passed while these 2 fixture diagnostics existed).
- `ruff format` / `ruff check`: clean. `py_compile`: clean on every touched production file. `node --check admin.js`: clean.
- Version bump: `pyproject.toml` 5.59.0 -> **5.60.0** (MINOR: new request-log column + admin-UI row = user-visible capability), `uv lock` regenerated in the same commit.

## Residual risks

- **The INSERT column/placeholder invariant has no dedicated guard test.** The bug was caught by the full suite, not by an assertion; a future column addition could reintroduce the same class of mismatch. A cheap static test (count columns vs placeholders in the INSERT string) would close it — not written here to keep the diff scoped.
- **R5 (OpenTelemetry `gen_ai.request.reasoning.level`) deliberately skipped:** `opentelemetry` is not a declared dependency and this repo's rules forbid adding undeclared deps. If wanted, it needs a dependency decision first.
- **R3 is a no-op today** (no models.dev entry publishes `reasoning_mandatory`). It lights up the day one does; until then the field is parsed-but-never-True in production.
- **The `reasoning_adaptation` column migration is additive** (`ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN`), same pattern as `requested_reasoning`. Old rows keep NULL forever, deliberately not backfilled — same reasoning as that column's migration comment.
- **`mandatory` parse lives before the options early-return** so bare `reasoning: true` entries still carry it; covered by the new `test_reasoning_mandatory_flag_is_parsed_and_silence_stays_unknown` (True / explicit False / absent -> None).

## Not done

- R5 OTel attribute (needs a dependency decision, above).
- R6 hybrid discovery, R7 response-side `ReasoningResult` normalization, R8 configurable rounding direction — deferred by the analysis's own ranking (large, or low-value-without-R2-style warnings).

commit.message:
feat(reasoning): R1 floor fix, R2 warn-and-downgrade, R3 mandatory handling, R4 dead-code removal

What was broken. R1: `_EFFORT_BUDGET_TOKENS` had MINIMAL/LOW at 512 - invalid
on Anthropic (hard floor 1024) and an outlier in the industry (LiteLLM,
OpenClaw, llmgateway, AI Proxy, Vercel all floor at 1024). R2: per-model
capability gating only emitted warnings to the server log, so a user who
asked for "max" and got "medium" had no way to learn why. R3: the OFF policy
was never rewritten for always-reasoning models (Claude Fable/Mythos, some
Grok), which either 400 outright or silently re-mapped off->low with no
signal. R4: `GeminiReasoningEncoder` in providers/google_openai/reasoning.py
was defined and re-exported but never instantiated anywhere - the shipped
Gemini provider uses a plain NamedEffortReasoning + apply_gemini_request_quirks.

The mechanism. R1: a one-line dict change for the floor (verified against
the file before writing). R2: `adapt_reasoning_policy` now returns
`tuple[ReasoningPolicy, ReasoningAdaptation]`; the `ReasoningAdaptation`
dataclass + `ReasoningAdaptationKind` StrEnum live in core/reasoning.py; the
adaptation threads through routing (RoutedMessagesRequest) -> capture
(request_capture.py) -> log (schema + migration + INSERT + read) -> export
(export.py) -> admin UI (admin.js Thinking pane) with a
`formatReasoningAdaptation` helper. R3: `mandatory: bool | None = None` on
`ModelReasoningCapability`, conservatively parsed from a conventional
`reasoning_mandatory` models.dev key (explicit-True only; absent means
unknown so the existing "unknown changes nothing" invariant holds), and a
new `_mandatory_off_rewrite` branch in gating that maps OFF -> lowest
supported effort (or adaptive when no vocabulary) with a SUBSTITUTED
warning. R4: the dead encoder + its exclusive helper + its re-export are
deleted; the test collateral (gemini branch in test_adaptive_reasoning.py,
the 35 gemini|* baseline keys) is cleaned to match.

What this PR also surfaces. The review-discipline gap that almost shipped:
a request-log INSERT with 43 columns but 42 `?` placeholders, so every
write silently failed (`Request log write failed: 42 values for 43
columns`) and cascaded ~260 test failures behind a file-scoped-green
facade. Caught only on the full-suite re-run after the touched suites all
passed. Lesson recorded in WORKING-NOTES 48: run the repo-wide checker
(ty check, pytest), not the file-scoped one; a written-rows invariant needs
a written-rows test in the verification set; count, don't type, mechanical
SQL.

Verification. Touched suites: 345/345 (test_reasoning_gating.py,
test_adaptive_reasoning.py, test_models_dev.py). Full suite: 5218 passed,
18 failed, 38 skipped - all 18 are the documented pre-existing set (16
PS1-installer / websearch-DDG / CI-script-suppression plus 2 env-dependent
websearch tests that pass with EXA_API_KEY stripped, the S22 class).
Full-repo ty check clean. Ruff format + check clean. py_compile clean on
every touched production file. node --check clean on admin.js.

Not done. R5 (OpenTelemetry gen_ai.request.reasoning.level) skipped: no
opentelemetry dep declared and the task rules forbid adding undeclared
deps. R3's mandatory rewrite is a no-op today (no models.dev entry
publishes reasoning_mandatory) - ship-as-ready, lights up the day one does.
